interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 25. The surgical findings included a Gleason 4+3, pT3a stage, positive surgical margins, and extraprostatic extension. Conversely, the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent, with no lymph node metastasis documented. The biopsy showed a higher grade (Gleason 4+4) than the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3). The nodal status was documented as no lymph node metastasis.

The primary driver for prognosis is the positive surgical margins and the higher preoperative Gleason score. Countervailing factors include the absence of lymph node metastasis and non-invasion of the seminal vesicles. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial in revising this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 42.09 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 33.67–50.51 months; its coverage has not been validated.
